title: feat(verify): the parent-derived write reach family, runnable as os verify --parent-write-reach (#15953 slice 4)
body:
Part of #15953
Clause-②: yes

## What this is

Slice 4 of #15953: the D half of the classification table's row 12 (comment 6115219467), plus the four acceptance notes slice 3's review left (6128105426). It adds the parent-derived write reach family to `@objectstack/verify`, runs it from `os verify --parent-write-reach` (opt-in), and documents it. Row 12's K residue (`sales_manager`'s grant) stays in hotcrm; its R residue (the spec gate on a hierarchy scope) belongs to `packages/spec` and is not in this PR. #15953 stays open for its remaining rows.

**Property, for any app.** ADR-0055 section 3 and its 2026-09-07 amendment: editing, deleting or creating a detail of a `controlled_by_parent` object requires edit access to its master, walked hop by hop to the first master that governs its own rows; the detail's own object permission is the first door. For a principal P, a detail record D under a master record M, and a verb (edit, delete, create), the write is expected admitted exactly when both halves hold:

- P holds the verb on D's object;
- P can edit M.

## The family (`packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.ts`)

- **Population.** Every object the spec's own parse (`ObjectSchema.safeParse`) declares `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'`, with exactly one `master_detail` field (ADR-0055 section 1), read through `referenceCarrierOf`. The chain is walked through each master's own parse until a master that governs its own rows.
- **Published sources each expectation is read from.**
  - The detail half: the server's effective object permissions for P (`GET /auth/me/permissions`, the one merge of the sets P holds, ADR-0124 D4), folded by `objectPermissionGrants` (`@objectstack/spec/security`). Nothing re-merges permission sets here.
  - The master half: MEASURED, never re-derived. An empty update of M as P, which runs every write gate M has (the object gate, the record gate, and for a master that is itself controlled by its parent the master gate above it) and changes no business value. Measured at REST first: an empty `PATCH` is refused by the object gate (no edit grant), by the record gate (edit grant, another owner, no all-records grant: `You do not have access to this record`) and by the master gate, and admitted on the caller's own record.
  - The rule: ADR-0055 section 3 and the amendment. No sharing, ownership, hierarchy or chain resolution is copied: the master half is the engine's own answer on M.
- **Door.** The engine's write as the signed-in principal: the handle's `hooks.run` with `as: token`, the `insert`, `update` by id and `delete` by id the REST data ingress makes, with the caller's context, the security middleware and the bound hooks included. See Deviations for why not the REST route itself. The system door bypasses authorization by design and is out of this family's population.
- **Principals.**
  - Three verifier personas whose permission sets the family authors from the app's own objects, registered at boot by `parentWriteReachSecurity(config)` and granted by name (ADR-0131 D3/D4, the RLS family's probe-persona path):
    - `master-all-records`: the root master by the all-records grant (`modifyAllRecords`), every verb on the details;
    - `detail-only`: the root master readable (`viewAllRecords`) but not editable, every verb on the details;
    - `master-all-records-no-delete`: the all-records grant, no delete on the details.
  - One persona per declared position, through the RLS family's exported `provisionRlsPositionPersona` and `declaredPositionNames`: its whole capability is what the app binds to the position.
  - The permission sets each persona holds are reported from the server's own answer.
- **Fixtures.** Reused `deriveCrudCases` / `fillRelationalRefs` and slice 3's required-fields fixture shape, through the seed door. Per persona, two master chains: one another principal owns (so the all-records grant, not ownership, is what is exercised) and one the persona owns. Under each, a detail another principal owns and one the persona owns.
- **Probes.** Per persona and master chain: the master read (a chain the persona cannot read is outside its reach, counted, not probed: a write to a record the caller cannot read is the RLS family's subject), the master's empty update, then edit and delete of each detail and one create.
- **Attribution.** A refusal holds only as `PERMISSION_DENIED` with status 403 whose `details` name the detail's object and the probed operation (`update`, `delete`, `insert`). Any other refusal (validation, a hook's own code, a refusal on another object) is `unattributed`. A write the door admits is checked on the record (an edit moves `updated_at`, a delete removes the row, a create holds the master), and a refusal whose record shows the write is contradicted.
- **Exclusions, with reasons, counted.** No `master_detail` field (the runtime would still derive through a required lookup, its own precedence, not compared here); two of them; a master the app does not declare; a cycle; a chain reaching the write gate's depth bound (eight controlled-by-parent masters, ADR-0055's amendment). Not derivable: the detail or a master in its chain cannot be synthesized.
- **Report.** Per object `proven` / `contradicted` / `failed` / `inconclusive` / `excluded` / `not-derivable`; per persona, run or not run with the reason. `summary.hardFailures` is `contradicted + failed` objects plus personas that could not be provisioned.

`os verify --parent-write-reach` boots its own fresh stack with `parentWriteReachSecurity(config)`, adds `parentWriteReach.summary.hardFailures` to the exit status, and emits `parentWriteReach` under `--json`. Without the flag, nothing changes.

## Finding: today's engine refuses every write to a detail two levels below its root master

On this tree's engine, a detail whose master is itself `controlled_by_parent` (a quote line under a quote under an account) is refused every edit, delete and create for every non-admin principal, with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, `master 'X' not editable by this user (row-level security)`, while the same principal's update of that middle master is admitted. This holds when the principal owns the whole chain and when it holds `modifyAllRecords` on both masters.

- Measured through REST on the fixture app: `PATCH /api/v1/data/pwr_quote/ID` with an empty body answers 200 and `PATCH /api/v1/data/pwr_quote_line/ID` answers 403, as the same principal.
- On hotcrm's real chain (`crm_quote_line_item` under `crm_quote` under `crm_account`), hotcrm's pinned 17.7.0 engine admits all 15 such writes for `sales_manager` and `sales_rep`; this tree's engine refuses all of them. A regression between the published 17.7.0 and this tree, not an app fact.
- The seam: ADR-0055's amendment says a detail whose whole chain is reachable stays writable; the hop runs `assertMasterRowEditable` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`) on the middle master, whose write filter re-read under the caller's context answers no row.

No engine change here, per the slice's ruling: the family reports it (`contradicted`), the fixture suite pins what the engine answers today (it flips to proven when the chain walk agrees with the middle master's own write), and the README and `cli.mdx` state that an app declaring such a chain fails `--parent-write-reach` until then. The report on #15953 carries it for filing.

## Evidence

**Fixture app** (`packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.test.ts`, `Tests 10 passed (10)`):

- Population (no boot): every exclusion with its reason, the chain hops, and the depth bound (eight controlled-by-parent masters above an object: excluded; seven: walked).
- Booted with `parentWriteReachSecurity`: 3 objects (two single-level, one two-level), 5 personas run (3 verifier, 2 position), 27 reaches probed, 3 outside the rep's read reach, 135 writes (54 edit, 54 delete, 27 create), 104 held. Both single-level objects proven for every persona under both master chains. The two-level object contradicted on 31 writes (the finding above), its refusals still held where the conjunction refuses.
- hotcrm's contract shape: the manager edits another principal's contract through the account by the all-records grant (detail another's and its own), is refused the delete (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, `details` `delete` on the contract, with the master's edit measured admitted, so the refusal is the contract's own permission), creates one; the rep reads none of another principal's accounts (outside its reach) and on its own account edits the master and is still refused every contract write (the object gate).
- **Negative controls** (no engine change):
  - a detail hook refusing every edit and delete with the platform's own envelope where the master is editable: contradicted on 4 of 4 writes per chain for `master-all-records`, held for `detail-only`;
  - a master hook refusing every edit of the master that way, so the master reads not editable while nothing stops its details: every detail write admitted and contradicted, for `master-all-records` on both chains.
- **Attribution control:** a refusal naming another object (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, `details` `update` on the account) and an app's own code (`RECORD_LOCKED`, 409) are `unattributed`, never held, never contradicted.
- A stack booted without `parentWriteReachSecurity` reports the three verifier personas not run, with the reason, counted in `hardFailures`; the position personas still run.

**CLI** (`packages/cli/test/verify-parent-write-reach.test.ts`, spawned, `Tests 3 passed (3)`): without the flag no `parentWriteReach` key and exit 0; with it the contract proven by 4 personas and exit 0; with a hook refusing the contract's edits with the platform envelope, contradicted, `hardFailures` 1, exit 1.

**Ablation of the family's own comparison** (`judge`), through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (wrap mode) inside a scratch script with `trap restore EXIT INT TERM` on absolute paths, at `8b4a5802f0` (first taken at `fa8171ea2c` with the same result). No build involved: the test imports the module by a relative path.

- **A.** `if (probe.expected === 'refused') return { outcome: 'held' };` replaced by an unconditional `held` plus the marker `ABLATION_15953_S4_A`. On disk: anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, blob `560c6d69` to `a6218f46`. RED: `Tests 4 failed | 6 passed (10)`: both negative controls, the two-level pin and the count that reads it. Restored: blob `560c6d69` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **B.** The same on `if (probe.expected === 'allowed') …` (marker `ABLATION_15953_S4_B`). On disk: anchor 1 to 0, blob `560c6d69` to `53cb38f1`. RED: `Tests 1 failed | 9 passed (10)`, exactly the second negative control. Restored to HEAD's blob, empty diff.
- Predicted direction for both: red. Observed: red.

**hotcrm, the first consumer.** Read-only clone at `1d7148bf`, fetched first: `main` is at `0f84c9c7`, and `test/contract-write-depth.test.ts` and every `controlled_by_parent` / permission declaration are unchanged there. The clone's `git status` stayed empty. `os verify` cannot boot hotcrm on this tree (protocol `^17.7.0` versus 18), so the family ran directly over slice 3's artifact (hotcrm's own CLI 17.7.0) and its `os migrate meta --from 17` snapshot (only `engines.protocol` moved to `^18`, and the 76 `email_template.category` tombstones the migration lists for hand application removed in memory).

| run | engine, hooks | personas run | proven | contradicted | inconclusive | excluded | writes (edit / delete / create) | held |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|
| A | hotcrm's pinned 17.7.0 `bootStack` over its own artifact, hooks live | 12 position (the 3 verifier personas not run: 17.7.0 has no `permission_set` grant column) | 4 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 70 / 70 / 35 | 137 |
| B | this tree, the snapshot with the artifact's 44 hook bodies grafted by name | 15 (3 verifier, 12 position) | 2 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 130 / 130 / 65 | 224 |
| C | this tree, the snapshot with hooks inert | 15 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 130 / 130 / 65 | 294 |

- **Proven:** `crm_contact` (A, B, C), `crm_quote` (A, B, C), `crm_opportunity_line_item` (A, C), `crm_contract` (C), `crm_quote_line_item` (A only: hotcrm's pinned engine).
- **Contradicted:** `crm_quote_line_item` on this tree, 31 writes in B and in C, for every persona that edits the quote (the finding above).
- **Inconclusive, with the app's own reasons:** `crm_contract` in A and B (hotcrm's `contract_validation` refuses a fixture whose term does not match its dates); `crm_opportunity_line_item` in B (its `opportunity_line_item_price_fill` hook refuses four creates on another object: `unattributed`, never read as the detail's own).
- **Excluded:** `crm_campaign_member`, `crm_event_attendee`, `crm_article_feedback` (no `master_detail` field; see the acceptance notes).
- 85 persona and master-chain pairs outside a persona's read reach in each run, counted, not probed.

**Against what row 12's D half asserted** (run C, every hotcrm hook inert; run B has the same verdicts where its fixtures could be written):

- "the manager changes the value of a contract standing in a rep's name" and "terminates it": `position:sales_manager` on a contract another principal owns, under an account another principal owns, reached by the all-records grant alone: edit allowed, held.
- "and still edits their OWN contract": the same, on a contract the manager owns: held.
- "the rep still cannot edit the contract they own — the object gate, unchanged": `position:sales_rep` edits its own account (measured admitted) and is refused every contract write with `PERMISSION_DENIED` naming the contract and the operation: held.
- "DELETE stays refused": the manager's delete refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `details` `delete` on `crm_contract`, while the manager's update of the account is measured admitted, so what refuses it is the contract's own permission lacking delete: held.
- 0 contradictions with what the file asserted. Its "does not leak to another object" describe (`crm_case`, not controlled by its parent) is outside this family.

## Carried acceptance notes (slice 3's review, 6128105426)

- **a. Attribution tightening** (`591513f0f5`). `judge` in `unique-scope.ts` reports a field-less unique refusal `unattributed` when a unique `indexes[]` entry covers the probed column, for insert and update. The control: a field whose own index cannot be created (the ADR-0120 D4 two-boot shape) beside a unique composite `indexes[{ fields: [name, kind], unique: 'organization' }]`. Before the change it read `proven`, 4 of 4 writes held with field-less refusals and admitted twins; after, `inconclusive`, 4 of 4 `unattributed`. The README's and the unreleased changeset's attribution sentences say so. The second twin was not built: the entry's other columns may be of any type, and `unattributed` is the safe reading.
- **b. `bootStack`'s input** (`a35a11217c`). One docblock sentence in `harness.ts` and one README sentence: the config is `defineStack` output; a raw object literal registers raw fields (an `autonumber` gets no unique and no index). No behaviour change.
- **c. The membership-policy sentence** (`aff59344f9`): the README names the `auth.membership_policy` setting beside `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY`.
- **d. The unreleased changeset** (`42d15b2d57`): "a sign-up that creates its own" is now `signUp`, then `POST /auth/organization/create`. `pre.json` lists no consumed changeset, so it was still unreleased. The same two sentences in `cli.mdx`'s `os verify` section take the a and d corrections too (`06ed55ddbe`).

## The pending release note this PR corrects

`check-empty-changeset` refuses this PR by design: it changes `.changeset/15953-verify-unique-scope-family.md`, which is on the merge base and was not added here. This is its DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, not a collision, so the file is not restored:

- the note is slice 3's own, for the same card, and still unreleased (`pre.json` lists no consumed changeset);
- this PR changes the behaviour it describes (carried note a): its attribution sentence said a field-less refusal is the field's once the twin is admitted, which is no longer true where a unique `indexes[]` entry covers the field;
- and it takes carried note d (`signUp`, then `POST /auth/organization/create`).

Both edits were ordered by the dispatch for this slice. Confirmation is requested here, as the gate asks; the gate stays red until then.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed (none is a reproducible defect through a public door, a contract violation or an authoring trap):

- The runtime and the lint accept a required `lookup` as a `controlled_by_parent` master (the third tier of `resolveCbpRelation` in plugin-security and of the lint's master candidates), which ADR-0055 section 1 and the spec's `sharingModel` docblock do not state. The family follows the spec and names those objects excluded: hotcrm's `crm_campaign_member`, `crm_event_attendee` and `crm_article_feedback`, 3 of its 8. Carrier: none.
- A generic fixture cannot satisfy every app rule: with hotcrm's hooks live, `contract_validation` refuses a contract whose term does not match its dates, so `crm_contract` reads inconclusive there and is proven with the hooks inert. Carrier: none.
- `fixtureBody` and its helpers are now copied in three family modules (delete-behavior, unique-scope, this one), each module-private. A shared one would live in `derive.ts`, outside this claim. Carrier: none.
- `provisionRlsPositionPersona` writes the reason "minted by `objectstack verify --rls`" on the position row it creates, whichever family calls it. Stored on an ephemeral stack only. Carrier: none.

## Deviations

- **The door.** PM mechanism assumption 5 named the REST data route; assumption 4 requires a refusal to name the detail object and the operation. Measured, the REST envelope cannot: it names the ROUTE's object on every refusal (an app hook refusing with another object named comes back naming the route's) and carries no operation. On hotcrm with hooks live that turned `crm_opportunity_line_item`'s `opportunity_line_item_price_fill` hook, refused on another object, into four false contradictions at REST. The family therefore writes through the engine as the signed-in principal, the three calls the REST ingress makes with the caller's context, where the refusal keeps its own `details`; there the same four read `unattributed`. The two-level finding was measured at REST as well.
- **Assumption 2's object-gate half** is read from the server's effective permissions (`/auth/me/permissions`), not re-merged from the declared sets: it is the one merge of the sets the principal holds (ADR-0124 D4), and a second copy of it is what ADR-0124 refuses.
- Conditional surfaces: two `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows (the gate asked); the `#22661` `CALLERS` row was not needed (the family never calls the reference-target arbiter; the core `repo` project is green without one).
- `origin/main` (`038d4c9588`, one commit, not on this surface) was merged before the PR, per AGENTS.md section 10; the build was refreshed and every suite and gate here ran on the merged tree.
- Commits carry the model-free trailer pair per AGENTS.md, and this body ends with its session-URL footer rather than the harness's own attribution form.
